sourceNote: Reviewed all supplied events, E0–E2174. The transcript contains recognition errors and several speaker changes inside single events; these mixed events are marked U. No audio or slides were supplied, and no edited teaser replays were identifiable. The retained text ends during audience questions.

candidates.speaker: A
candidates.quote: those who deny it do so on the basis of theological or philosophical assumptions
candidates.explanation: Craig adopts a scholar's characterization that locates empty-tomb denial in prior assumptions, potentially discounting objections without examining them. However, E381–431 supply historical considerations and scholarly testimony. The passage does not explicitly say every historical objection must be disregarded, so categorical protection is uncertain; this is not an unsupported catchphrase.

candidates.speaker: A
candidates.quote: draw near to God and He will draw near to you
candidates.explanation: The promise extends experiential testimony into an assurance that sincere seeking succeeds, without explaining unsuccessful sincere searches. It could make failure attributable to insufficient seeking, but Craig does not explicitly draw that inference. E444–460 distinguish experience from argument, and E1914–1923 later acknowledge reasons that could undermine experiential belief.

candidates.speaker: A
candidates.quote: we're simply not in a position to say whether or not the pain and suffering in the world
candidates.explanation: Unseen consequences across centuries and countries, possibly maximizing salvation, become grounds for denying that observed suffering can support the comparative objection (E1236–1257). The missing bridge is from possible hidden goods to suspension of that evidential comparison. Chaos theory supplies an analogy, making this a protective argument rather than a slogan.

candidates.speaker: A
candidates.quote: I would go through it a million million times over to know this joy and happiness
candidates.explanation: Unlimited future blessedness is invoked to place earthly suffering in perspective and weaken its evidential force, without establishing why permitting the harm was necessary. This protection is expressly limited to sufferers who trusted God (E1284–1286). The imagined retrospective statement illustrates a compensation argument; it is not independently offered as a slogan.

candidates.speaker: A
candidates.quote: Comfort is available to those I believe who seek God
candidates.explanation: The assurance answers absent comfort by distinguishing seekers from intellectual assenters. Reports that some Christians receive comfort (E1300–1303) do not establish availability to every seeker. Yet Craig says 'I believe' and 'often,' without expressly declaring uncomforted victims insincere. Draper's blame interpretation at E1479–1494 does not itself establish that protective inference.

contrasts.speaker: A
contrasts.quote: in the absence of any good reasons to doubt my experience
contrasts.explanation: Craig explicitly conditions trust in religious experience on lacking good reasons for doubt. He disputes whether the objections supplied defeat his experience, leaving criticism relevant rather than declaring experience immune.

contrasts.speaker: B
contrasts.quote: of course we don't know that there is all these other universes
contrasts.explanation: Draper offers multiple universes as a possible limitation on fine-tuning evidence, acknowledges that their existence is unknown, and retains some evidential force for Craig's argument.
